title: Adam Air 574
summary: Adam Air Flight 574, a Boeing 737-400, crashed into the Makassar Strait on 1 January 2007 with all 102 people aboard killed. The flight crew became preoccupied with troubleshooting an inertial navigation system anomaly. While attempting to reset the IRS, the first officer inadvertently disconnected the autopilot, and neither pilot noticed the disconnect. The aircraft entered a slow right bank, and when the bank angle warning sounded, the crew did not recognize the autopilot disconnect and the aircraft entered an uncontrolled descent into the sea.
probable_cause: This accident resulted from a combination of factors, including the failure of the pilots to adequately monitor the aircraft following an inadvertent autopilot disconnect during IRS troubleshooting. Previous maintenance issues involving the aircraft's ailerons caused the airplane to slowly roll to the right, and the pilots did not notice or arrest the descent before impacting the sea.

title: 2007 Balad aircraft crash

Aircraft crashed at 0700 UTC, about 2.5 km away from Balad Air Base while attempting to land. One eyewitness said he watched a missile strike the right fuselage; other eyewitness also reported seeing aircraft shot down. Officials claim crash caused by poor weather conditions.

title: Garuda Indonesia 200
summary: Garuda Indonesia Flight 200, a Boeing 737-400 with 152 aboard, crashed during landing at Adisucipto Airport on March 7, 2007 after the captain conducted an unstabilized approach at excessive speed. The aircraft touched down 860 meters beyond the runway threshold at 221 knots, 87 knots faster than normal landing speed. The captain ignored repeated warnings from the copilot and aircraft systems, and the copilot failed to take control despite policy requirements. The aircraft overran the runway, crashed into a rice field, and caught fire.
probable_cause: The pilot in command flew an unstabilized approach with excessive descent rate and airspeed, ignored warnings from the copilot and aircraft systems, and continued the landing. The first officer failed to take control as required by policy due to inadequate training.

title: 2007 Mogadishu TransAVIAexport Airlines Il-76 crash
summary: A Belarusian Ilyushin Il-76 cargo aircraft operated by TransAVIAexport Airlines departed Mogadishu International Airport on March 23, 2007, at 14:00 local time bound for Minsk with a refueling stop in Djibouti. The aircraft was carrying equipment and humanitarian aid for repairing another Il-76 damaged by an earlier shootdown attempt. As the aircraft reached approximately 10,000 feet altitude, the pilot reported a problem in engine number two and requested an emergency return to the airport. While attempting to return, one wing suddenly exploded and separated from the aircraft, falling into the Indian Ocean, while the fuselage continued burning along the beach at low altitude before crashing near Kuluweyne. All 11 crew members, all Belarusian, were killed. Investigators confirmed the aircraft was shot down by missile fire during the Battle of Mogadishu.

title: Kenya Airways 507
summary: The aircraft departed Douala at 00:06 local time without seeking takeoff clearance from the control tower. Once airborne, the aircraft developed a right bank tendency which the captain initially controlled. After 24 seconds at 1,000 feet, the captain let go of the control wheel and called for autopilot engagement, but the first officer did not acknowledge the command and the autopilot did not engage. For 55 seconds neither pilot nor autopilot controlled the aircraft, which gradually increased its bank angle to 34 degrees when the bank angle warning sounded. The captain's corrective inputs aggravated the situation, and with the aircraft banking at 115 degrees right at 2,290 feet, the crew could not recover.
probable_cause: The aircraft departed without receiving clearance from air traffic control. The autopilot did not engage due to lack of acknowledgment from the copilot. The pilots failed to detect the increasing bank angle until it became critical, and used opposite and conflicting control inputs that prevented recovery.

title: PMTair 241
summary: PMTair Flight 241, an Antonov An-24, departed Siem Reap for Sihanoukville on 25 June 2007. As the aircraft approached its destination in deteriorating weather, the crew deviated from the assigned route without informing ATC, continued descent below radar coverage in instrument conditions, and crashed into terrain near Bokor Mountain. The investigation concluded that the crew's decision to continue descent in inclement weather and poor management from PMTair contributed to the accident.

summary: TAM Airlines Flight 3054, an Airbus A320-233 flying from Porto Alegre, overran runway 35L at São Paulo's Congonhas Airport on 17 July 2007 after touching down in moderate rain with the right thrust reverser deactivated and the runway freshly resurfaced but without water-channeling grooves. The aircraft failed to slow down normally, veered left, crossed Avenida Washington Luís, and crashed into a TAM Express warehouse and gas station, exploding on impact and killing all 187 people aboard plus 12 on the ground. CENIPA concluded the accident was caused by pilot error during the landing.
probable_cause: CENIPA concluded that the accident was caused by pilot error during the landing at São Paulo; flight data showed both thrust levers remained in the CL (climb) position at touchdown despite the 'retard, retard' aural warning, and the aircraft overran the ungrooved, rain-slicked runway.

factors.evidence: The Airbus A320 overran runway 35L after touching down during moderate rain, and a slope prevented the drainage of accumulated water on the asphalt.
The resurfacing work was completed on 29 June, but the grooves were not added, and there were no runway-end safety areas.
Despite the aircraft touching down without incident, it did not slow down normally, veering to the left as it departed the far end at around 90 kn.
Immediately prior to touchdown, both thrust levers were in CL (or 'climb') position, and an aural warning, 'retard, retard,' was issued advising the pilots to retard the thrust lever.
The aircraft's momentum carried it over traffic on Avenida Washington Luís and crushed a four-storey TAM Express facility.

events.text: Two seconds prior to touchdown, an aural warning, 'retard, retard,' was issued by the flight's computer system, advising the pilots to retard the thrust lever to the recommended idle position.
The flight data recorder showed that immediately prior to touchdown, both thrust levers were in CL (climb) position, with engine power governed by the autothrottle system.
Despite touching down without incident, the aircraft did not slow down normally, veering to the left as it departed the far end of the runway at around 90 kn.
The aircraft's momentum carried it over traffic on Avenida Washington Luís and crushed a four-storey TAM Express facility adjacent to a gas station, resulting in a large fire.

title: 2007 Phoenix news helicopter collision
summary: Two AS-350 AStar helicopters operating news coverage of a Phoenix police pursuit collided at 12:46 p.m. MST on 27 July 2007 over Steele Indian School Park. The NTSB investigation concluded that both pilots failed to see and avoid the other helicopter. Contributing factors included high workload from concurrent reporting duties and the lack of formal procedures for coordinating air operations among Phoenix news helicopters. All four occupants were killed.
probable_cause: Both pilots' failure to see and avoid the other helicopter. Contributing factors were the pilots' responsibility to perform concurrent reporting and visual tracking duties that distracted from collision avoidance, and the absence of formal procedures for news helicopter operations in Phoenix airspace.

title: China Airlines 120
summary: A China Airlines Boeing 737-800 caught fire at the gate shortly after landing at Naha Airport. During slat retraction, a downstop assembly that had detached during maintenance punctured the wing fuel tank. Fuel leaked onto the tarmac and ignited when contacting the hot right engine, causing explosions and fire. All occupants evacuated safely with only minor injuries.
probable_cause: A maintenance procedure to prevent nut loosening resulted in loss of the washer, causing the downstop assembly to fall off and puncture the fuel tank during slat retraction.

The leaked fuel ignited on contact with high-temperature areas on the right engine after aircraft stopped at the gate.
The maintenance procedure did not include verification that the washer remained properly secured after assembly.

title: One-Two-GO Airlines 269
summary: One-Two-GO Airlines Flight 269 crashed into an embankment beside runway 27 during a go-around after an aborted landing attempt. Both pilots had exceeded legal duty time limits, and the First Officer's attempt to transfer control to the Captain was not acknowledged. The aircraft's engines remained at idle for 13 seconds during climb.

title: Atlasjet 4203
summary: Atlasjet Flight 4203, an MD-83 with 57 aboard, crashed near Isparta, Turkey on November 30, 2007 during approach. The GPWS was malfunctioning and its malfunction was not properly logged. The aircraft was equipped with the more sophisticated instrument landing system. While turning to align with the runway, the aircraft deviated 30 degrees from the intended flight path and headed away from the runway toward north instead of northeast.
probable_cause: The crew executed an instrument approach with a malfunctioning GPWS, deviated from the assigned flight path by 30 degrees, and descended into terrain while believing they were on the correct approach.

factors.evidence: GPWS had been malfunctioning during at least 85 of last 234 flights and was not properly logged in maintenance records despite known malfunction.

Assuming they were on course, the crew descended further while aircraft was flying away from runway toward north.
Aircraft crashed in vicinity of Keçiborlu approximately 12 km west of destination airport while descending during failed approach.

events.text: Flight 4203 took off from Istanbul Atatürk Airport at 00:51 EET with 50 passengers and 7 crew members aboard.
